title: Feed v0.2.3
content:
Feed now has a richer manual-entry editor for public notes and changelog-adjacent updates. This pass focused on making manual posts easier to compose directly in the browser, while keeping release notes, GitHub-imported entries, and the existing weekly feed structure intact.

What changed:

  • Rich manual composer: Manual entries can now be written with inline formatting, headings, lists, blockquotes, and direct link insertion instead of relying only on plain text or markdown-style previewing.
  • Image and attachment uploads: The editor can upload images and general attachments through the protected Feed API, insert them into the post body, and preserve them when entries are edited later.
  • Safer stored HTML: Manual content is sanitized before publishing so the feed can support richer posts while stripping unsafe markup and keeping uploaded media links stable.
  • Pinned-post visual layer: Pinned entries now have their own light-blue card treatment with a separate computer-pattern overlay, making them feel intentionally promoted without blending into the main page background.

This gives Feed a stronger authoring layer for future public notes, project writeups, and screenshot-heavy updates while preserving the current versioned release workflow.
